name: proscraper
what_it_holds: MIT CLI wrapper around SerpAPI (a paid API) covering Google Hotels, Flights, Scholar, TripAdvisor, with SQLite persistence and response caching for repeated pulls. 0 stars, updated Aug 2026.
why_useful: The SQLite caching layer is the one design here that would actually accumulate a point-in-time price panel over repeated runs rather than discarding each pull, if paired with a paid SerpAPI key; illustrates a workable architecture even though no data or key is provided.
themes: Google Hotel Ads / Google Travel price datasets and scrapers; hotel metasearch price panels

name: hotel-rate-shopper
what_it_holds: MIT repo (0 stars, updated Aug 2026) tracking Booking.com rates over time for competitive rate-intelligence/RM use, not Google specifically. No committed dataset found in listing (description only).
why_useful: Adjacent metasearch-style rate-tracking method (Booking.com rather than Google) that explicitly frames itself as tracking rates 'over time' — closest thing found to an actual time-series rate panel design, but appears to be a fresh/empty tool rather than a populated dataset.

name: Veetal-Connect/recipes
what_it_holds: MIT 'recipes' repo (0 stars, updated 2 Sep 2026) of Node scripts against the Veetal Connect commercial API: hotel rate shopping, multi-OTA reputation, rate parity, event demand, flight data. Recipes only, no data committed, requires a paid Veetal API key.
why_useful: Confirms rate-parity / multi-OTA rate-shopping as a commercially served category (paid API) rather than something with open committed data; the 'event demand' recipe name is a minor pointer to event-driven hotel demand signals (gap 11) but content is not inspectable without a key.

name: booking-hotels-prices-scraper
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed scraper claiming to pull live nightly hotel rates, reviews and availability from Booking.com for any destination/dates without an API key or partner account. No committed data files observed (repo not opened beyond listing); README-level description only.
why_useful: If it works, could be a source of Booking.com listed-rate/ADR data as a non-STR alternative-accommodation comparator (gap #9), but it targets traditional hotels on Booking.com, not RevPAR/STR-panel data, and running it against a live commercial site is a ToS question we are not authorized to make.
themes: Hotel performance data: STR / CoStar weekly and monthly US RevPAR figures scraped from press releases, HotStats, Smith Travel history compiled on GitHub

name: Africa Mauritius Hotel Room Occupancy Rate datasets (electricsheepafrica)
what_it_holds: Five small Hugging Face dataset cards from the electricsheepafrica org (part of a larger pan-African open-statistics project): 'Africa Mauritius Hotel Room Occupancy Rate' at all-hotels and large-hotels granularity, and quarterly/monthly cuts, ~10-60 rows each, sourced from Mauritius national statistics, updated Aug 2026, covering roughly 2019-2023. No linked GitHub pipeline repo could be confirmed from the org page.
why_useful: Genuine, government-sourced hotel occupancy time series (not synthetic/Kaggle), which is rare to find at all on open platforms — but it is Mauritius only, a market irrelevant to ABNB's segment mix, and very short/low-frequency. Cataloguing as a proof that national-statistics-office hotel occupancy series do get mirrored onto HF/GitHub by these scraping projects; worth a look for whether the same org/pipeline covers a bigger STR-relevant country (not confirmed).
duplicate_of_holding: Distinct from our Hawaii DBEDT series (different country) but same category (national hotel-occupancy statistics office data)
